Neighboring overlaps compare states, and closing the loop cancels the independently chosen endpoint phases. The Berry phase records this sequence of comparisons, not a direct sum of arbitrary wavefunction phases. The connection A describes infinitesimal neighboring-state comparisons and depends on local phase conventions; curvature describes the growth of a sufficiently small loop phase with oriented area.
